interface.title: Lab Results → DIGGS
interface.stage_of_work: Data reporting and exchange: moving finished lab test results into the project's DIGGS 3 subsurface data file
interface.what_it_is_for: A single offline page that takes a soil lab's results workbook (or CSVs), checks it, and writes a DIGGS 3 XML file. It either adds the results to the borings and samples in an existing project DIGGS file or builds a new DIGGS file from boring coordinates the user types in.

data.note: 'Try it with example data' loads example_project.xml (2 borings, B-1 and B-2, both with locations, and 2 samples) plus an example workbook with 12 sheets (Project, Samples, Water Content, Atterberg Limits, Atterberg Trials, Wash 200, Gradation, Specific Gravity, Unit Weight, Organic Content, Compaction, Corrosion). Together they give 14 tests on 6 samples. No test files were available to upload (browser_list_files is empty), and the page's own downloads cannot be given back to it, so the workbook and DIGGS-file drop zones were only opened, never filled. The build panel's boring count tile reads 1 while the loaded file has 2 borings; the run did not find out why.

features.name: Reference-file summary with location-status flag
features.general: Load a reference dataset, see a count summary of what it holds, and mark how final its coordinates are so the output carries that status
features.specific: The DIGGS file card shows counts of borings, borings with locations and samples, plus the boring IDs. An 'as drilled / proposed' radio adds an amber warning and a PROPOSED-locations remark in the output's audit trail. Remove switches the page to the from-scratch path.
steps: load the project file (or the example)
read the boring, location and sample counts and the boring list
choose as drilled or proposed
remove the file to switch to the from-scratch path

Rebuild the export after changing the location status and the set of tables

features.name: Data-entry template generated from the reference file
features.general: Produce a data-entry template pre-listing the locations and specimens already held in a reference dataset
features.specific: 'Download a workbook for this project (.xlsx)' on the DIGGS file card downloads <file>_lab_workbook.xlsx. Its contents were not opened in this run.
steps: load the project file (or the example)
choose as drilled or proposed
press Download a workbook for this project (.xlsx)
serves_tasks: Generate a data-entry template listing the project's existing locations and specimens

features.name: Merge into an existing file with sample matching
features.general: Attach new results to the specimens already recorded in a reference dataset, add any specimens it lacks under new IDs, and record who added them in an audit trail
features.specific: Step 5 reports how many workbook samples were found in the DIGGS file ('2 of 6 samples found in example_project.xml; 4 will be added'). Tests on matched samples point to the file's own sample IDs (sampleRef #SMP_B_1_S_1); unmatched samples are added with LAB_ IDs; an audit-trail remark records the lab and the location status. The matching rule itself (by name, or by depth interval) was not tested.
steps: load the project DIGGS file and the results workbook
read the sample-matching line in the build panel
open Preview the XML to see sampleRefs to existing samples and new LAB_ samples
check the audit-trail remark, then download
serves_tasks: Attach the results to the existing project's locations and specimens, and export

features.name: Multi-sheet intake table with per-sheet template override
features.general: Bring in several tables at once, let the tool guess what each one is, override the guess per table, drop tables, and see the change in the output right away
features.specific: Step 3 lists every workbook sheet or CSV with a 'Read as' dropdown (Auto, or one of 13 templates), a row count and Remove. A wrong template triggers a required-column error that disables the download, and removing a sheet updates the test counts.

It has a collapsible 'Preview the XML' that updates live with unit changes, a File name box and Download DIGGS XML. The boring count tile read 1 with a 2-boring file loaded (unexplained).
